dedupe_keys.name: temoa tools for energy model optimization and analysis

description: Temoa (Tools for Energy Model Optimization and Analysis) is an open-source energy system optimisation framework for long-term planning of technology investment and operation. It is developed by the TemoaProject team, with its reference paper by Kevin Hunter, Sarat Sreepathi and Joseph F. DeCarolis in Energy Economics (2013), and a 2019 study by Anderson Rodrigo de Queiroz and Joseph DeCarolis repurposed it for seasonal power generation planning on the IEEE 24-bus system. The framework supports perfect foresight, myopic planning, uncertainty analysis and generation of alternative solutions. Users install it from PyPI, create a tutorial configuration and SQLite database with one command and run the model from a command-line interface, and the package is organised into a public API, command-line tools, model components and constraints, and data input and output modules. Coverage is not tied to a place; users supply regional data. The code is accessible on GitHub and PyPI under the MIT licence at no cost, and is actively developed (version 4 releases, 14 tags, latest commit September 2026). Caveats: the 2019 Zenodo archive holds an older operational branch under GPL 2.0, and users need a linear programming solver. Simulation uses are capacity expansion and scenario analysis of energy systems under uncertainty. Related records: model-switch and model-oemof-solph are comparable open planning models.
